title: 2001 AMC 8 Problem 16
statement: A square piece of paper, \(4\) inches on a side, is folded in half vertically. Both layers are then cut in half parallel to the fold. Three new rectangles are formed, a large one and two small ones. What is the ratio of the perimeter of one of the small rectangles to the perimeter of the large rectangle?

solutions.text:
The square is folded in half to create a \(4\times2\) rectangle.

Cutting the folded paper in half parallel to the fold gives two small \(4\times1\) rectangles and one large \(4\times2\) rectangle.

The ratio of the perimeter of a small rectangle to the perimeter of the large rectangle is \[\frac{2(4+1)}{2(4+2)}=\frac{10}{12}=\frac56.\]

Thus, E is the correct answer.
hints: After folding, the paper is a \(4\times2\) rectangle
